raw_record.support_text: The long-term carcinogenicity study of phenytoin in F344/DuCrj rats (0, 0.025, 0.05% in diet for 2 yr) found no statistically significant increase in the incidence of any particular tumour type and no evidence of accelerated tumour induction in any phenytoin-treated group. All neoplasms observed were histologically similar to known spontaneous tumours of this strain. It was concluded that phenytoin had no carcinogenic potential in F344 rats under the conditions used.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: 2-yr dietary administration at 0.025% and 0.05% in male and female rats; all tumours histologically similar to known spontaneous tumours of the strain
raw_record.extra_details: Dose-related decrease in mean body weight in treated females; survival similar to controls; study performed because of inadequacy of previous rat investigations.

raw_record.support_text: Limited long-term oral studies in rats indicated a low toxicity for propyl paraben and have generated no evidence of carcinogenic activity. In short-term oral studies, forestomach changes were reported in two rat studies, but in other studies in rats and hamsters, no changes were noted. Propyl paraben was not mutagenic in Ames bacterial and yeast tests.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Based on limited long-term oral studies; forestomach changes seen in short-term oral studies in two rat studies but not in other rat or hamster studies
raw_record.extra_details: Propyl paraben showed low acute oral toxicity (LD50 >8000 mg/kg in some studies) and was not mutagenic in Ames bacterial and yeast tests. A negative carcinogenicity finding in the limited long-term rat oral studies.

The estimation of THQ and TTHQ suggested ingestion of trace metals through Hilsa shad consumption was safe, and there was no evidence of carcinogenic risk for consumers based on the TR value evaluation of the metals As, Pb, Cd, and Ni from Hilsa shad consumption.

raw_record.extra_details: TR (target cancer risk) value showed no carcinogenic risk; EDI, THQ, TTHQ also indicated no risk to human health from consuming Hilsa fish.

raw_record.support_text: Reexamination by the NTP of the NCI Study I of malathion in Osborne-Mendel rats diagnosed two additional thyroid follicular cell adenomas, causing the previously reported marginal positive trend to disappear. The evaluation attendant with both the original and subsequent pathology diagnoses was the same: under the conditions of these studies there was no evidence of carcinogenicity in male or female Osborne-Mendel rats receiving time-weighted average doses of 4700 or 8150 ppm malathion in their diet for 80 weeks.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Time-weighted average dietary doses of 4700 or 8150 ppm for 80 weeks.
raw_record.extra_details: NCI Technical Report No. 24 (NCI, 1978). Original report noted a marginal positive trend (P=0.026; 0/46, 0/48, 4/49) for follicular cell adenoma or carcinoma of the thyroid gland that disappeared after NTP-identified additional diagnoses.

raw_record.support_text: In its 2016 re-evaluation under Regulation (EC) No 257/2010, the EFSA ANS Panel concluded that, based on the data available at that time, E 171 (titanium dioxide) when used as a food additive did not raise concern with respect to genotoxicity and that it was not carcinogenic after oral administration. A margin of safety was calculated from the NOAEL of 2,250 mg TiO2/kg bw per day identified from a carcinogenicity study in rats.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Conclusion from the 2016 EFSA ANS Panel re-evaluation, based on the toxicological data available at that time.
raw_record.extra_details: A NOAEL of 2,250 mg TiO2/kg bw per day was identified from a carcinogenicity study in rats and used to calculate a margin of safety. This prior conclusion was context for the current updated assessment of E 171.

condition_text: Single large dose produces kidney tumors; repeated small doses instead produce liver tumors

raw_record.support_text: The method of dosage with dimethylnitrosamine (DMN) can profoundly alter the incidence of tumors. Repeated small doses lead to a high incidence of liver tumors, but large single doses produce kidney tumors. There is a correlation between the induction of kidney tumors by a single large dose of DMN and the persistence of O6-methylguanine in DNA.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Single large dose produces kidney tumors; repeated small doses instead produce liver tumors
raw_record.extra_details: Kidney tumor induction correlates with slower elimination and persistence of O6-methylguanine in kidney DNA; liver generates the methylating species about eight times more than kidney.

condition_text: Intramuscular injection into both thighs; 2.5 mg Ni3S2 (31 µmol Ni) per site as aqueous suspension (0.2 ml/site); 66-week experiment; injection-site tumor effect.

raw_record.support_text: In the carcinogenicity study, 20 male F344/NCr rats per group received i.m. injections of Ni3S2 (2.5 mg, 31 µmol Ni) per site as aqueous suspensions. At necropsy 19/19 rats given i.m. Ni3S2 alone developed injection-site sarcomas (rhabdomyosarcoma, fibrosarcoma, histiocytic, undifferentiated), with bilateral sarcomas in 3/19 and metastases to the lung in 11 rats; no water-injection control rat developed a muscle tumor.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Intramuscular injection into both thighs; 2.5 mg Ni3S2 (31 µmol Ni) per site as aqueous suspension (0.2 ml/site); 66-week experiment; injection-site tumor effect.
raw_record.extra_details: Tumor incidence 19/19 treated rats; bilateral sarcomas in 3/19; metastases to lung (11 rats) and kidney (1 rat); one rat with an undifferentiated sarcoma at ventral spine and one preputial gland adenoma; water-injection controls 0/20. Intramuscular Ni3S2 combined with ZnO or ZnAcet reduced the carcinoma incidence (14-20/20).

condition_atoms: reported_condition=rat-specific effect with low clinical relevance; cck has no mitogenic effect in mice, non-human primates or humans. developed from exocrine pancreatic hyperplasia at 12 months to exocrine pancreatic neoplasia by 24 months. tumours increased at all doses
condition_group: reported_condition=rat-specific effect with low clinical relevance; cck has no mitogenic effect in mice, non-human primates or humans. developed from exocrine pancreatic hyperplasia at 12 months to exocrine pancreatic neoplasia by 24 months. tumours increased at all doses+route=oral+species=rat
condition_text: Rat-specific effect with low clinical relevance; CCK has no mitogenic effect in mice, non-human primates or humans. Developed from exocrine pancreatic hyperplasia at 12 months to exocrine pancreatic neoplasia by 24 months. Tumours increased at all doses.

raw_record.support_text: In the rat carcinogenicity study there was an increase in pancreatic tumours at all doses. Pancreatic changes began as exocrine pancreatic hyperplasia at 12 months and developed to exocrine pancreatic neoplasia by 24 months; mechanistically this follows HP-β-CD complexing bile acids, increasing cholecystokinin (CCK), which acts as a mitogen in the rat. These pancreatic tumours are considered a rat-specific effect with low clinical relevance because CCK has no mitogenic effect in mice, non-human primates and man.
raw_record.qualifying_conditions: Rat-specific effect with low clinical relevance; CCK has no mitogenic effect in mice, non-human primates or humans. Developed from exocrine pancreatic hyperplasia at 12 months to exocrine pancreatic neoplasia by 24 months. Tumours increased at all doses.
raw_record.extra_details: Mechanism attributed to HP-β-CD complexing bile acids leading to increased cholecystokinin (CCK), a mitogen producing increased proliferation of acinar cells in rat exocrine pancreas.

raw_record.support_text: Group II rats were induced with liver cancer by giving 0.01% DEN in drinking water for 16 weeks. Nodules and hepatic tumors were subsequently classified in the liver of treated rats, with hepatic tumors characterized by severe disturbance of normal hepatic structure with anastomosing atypical trabeculae or glandular arrangement.
raw_record.extra_details: Induction with 0.01% DEN in drinking water for 16 weeks; used to establish a liver cancer model. Nodules and hepatic tumors were classified according to Bannasch and Zerban (1990).

raw_record.support_text: Suspicions of a link between chromium exposure and lung cancer were first raised in the late nineteenth century, when increased incidence was observed among Scottish chrome pigment workers. It was only in the 1980s that Cr, more specifically Cr(VI), was firmly established as a human lung carcinogen.
raw_record.extra_details: Cr(VI) specifically, as opposed to Cr generally, was firmly established as a human lung carcinogen in the 1980s; first suspicions raised in the late nineteenth century among Scottish chrome pigment workers.
